t: You're looking at Tate Britain, the art museum on Millbank, which holds the art of the United Kingdom since Tudor times. It was founded by Sir Henry Tate, the sugar merchant and philanthropist, and the original gallery was designed by the architect Sidney R. J. Smith, who did much work for Tate. The collection has large holdings of J. M. W. Turner, who left all his own work to the nation. The building was known as the National Gallery of British Art from 1897 and as the Tate Gallery from 1932, before taking its present name in 2000. The art historian Rosa Schapire died here.
